t.1.105.1: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Endowed with beauty, strength of character and virtue, delighting in dharma and great in her vows, was the daughter of Kuntibhoja, when a svayaṃvara had been arranged by her father.
t.1.105.2: In the midst of thousands of kings she found Pāṇḍu, lion-fanged, with shoulders like an elephant's, bull-eyed and mighty in strength.
t.1.105.3: That joy of the Kurus, of boundless good fortune, was united with the daughter of Kuntibhoja, like Maghavan with Paulomī.
t.1.105.5: She was renowned among all kings, unequalled in beauty on earth; purchased then for Pāṇḍu's sake with great wealth, she was given in marriage, for Bhīṣma arranged the wedding of the great-souled Pāṇḍu.
t.1.105.6: Seeing Pāṇḍu, that tiger among men, lion-chested, with shoulders like an elephant's and eyes like a bull's, high-minded, the men on earth were filled with wonder.
t.1.105.4: Devavrata, too, went to the city of the Madras, and by him was obtained Mādrī, the daughter of the lord of the Madras, renowned throughout the three worlds.
t.1.105.7: Then Pāṇḍu, his marriage accomplished, endowed with strength and energy, set out against his many enemies, eager to conquer the earth.
t.1.105.8: First, setting out, Pāṇḍu, the lion among men who upheld the glory of the Kauravas, conquered in battle the Daśārṇas, who had committed offenses.
t.1.105.9: Then Pāṇḍu, taking with him an army bearing banners of many kinds, abounding in elephants, horses and chariots, and crowded with throngs of foot soldiers,
t.1.105.10: The offender against all heroes, the enemy of all kings, Dārva, protector of the kingdom of Magadha, was slain in Rājagṛha.
t.1.105.11: Then, taking with him his treasury, his mounts and his troops, Pāṇḍu went to Mithilā, and the Videhas were conquered by him in battle.
t.1.105.12: Likewise among the Kāśis, the Suhmas and the Puṇḍras, O bull of the Bharatas, he won glory for the Kurus by the valor and strength of his own arms.
t.1.105.13: Encountering that tamer of foes, the fire that was Pāṇḍu, whose great flames were floods of arrows and whose blazing rays were his weapons, the kings were burned up.
t.1.105.14: Those kings together with their armies, their forces shattered by Pāṇḍu who was accompanied by his own army, were made subject to his will and set to the tasks of paying tribute.
t.1.105.15: All those kings of the earth, every one of them, were conquered by him; they regarded him as the one true hero, like Puraṃdara among the gods.
t.1.105.16: All the lords of the earth, bowing low with joined palms, approached him, bringing wealth and jewels of many kinds.
t.1.105.18: Donkeys, camels and buffaloes, and whatever goats and sheep there were, all of that the king, lord of Nāgapura, accepted.
t.1.105.19: Taking that wealth, Pāṇḍu went back again with his mounts rejoicing, intending to gladden his own kingdoms and the city named after the elephant.
t.1.105.17: Gems, pearls and coral, gold and silver as well, the choicest cattle, the choicest horses, the choicest chariots, and elephants.
t.1.105.20: The fame-born renown of Śaṃtanu, that lion among kings, and of the wise Bharata, which had been lost, was raised up again by Pāṇḍu.
t.1.105.21: Those who in former times had seized the kingdoms of the Kurus and the wealth of the Kurus were made to pay tribute by Pāṇḍu, the lion of Nāgapura.
t.1.105.22: Thus spoke the kings and the ministers of the king, gathered together, glad and with joyful hearts, along with the townspeople and the country folk.
t.1.105.23: All of them, headed by Bhīṣma, went out to meet him as he arrived. Having gone only a short way along the road, those dwellers of Nāgapura, delighted, saw the land covered with people of many kinds.
t.1.105.25: He who increased the joy of Kausalyā, having saluted his father's feet, also honored the townspeople and the country folk as each deserved.
t.1.105.24: Coming upon the treasures, high and low, brought in on many kinds of vehicles, along with the finest elephants, horses and chariots, and the cows, camels and sheep, the Kauravas together with Bhīṣma could see no end to them.
t.1.105.26: Bhīṣma, meeting his son as he returned again, his aim accomplished after crushing the kingdoms of others, shed tears for joy.
t.1.105.27: With the great sounds of hundreds of massed instruments and of kettledrums, he entered the city named after the elephant, delighting the citizens on every side.
